claim_tested: B9D2 retains the C2 Ca2+-ligand cluster
key_finding: Core RMSD 1.54-1.67 A to four Ca2+-bound C2 domains over 50-76 Calpha; 7 of 8 mapped Ca2+ ions fall in one 6 A cluster; B9D2 has 2 carboxylate O within 8 A vs median 9.5 for Ca2+-dependent C2 (Mann-Whitney p=0.0092)
context: human B9D2 AlphaFold model, mean pLDDT 89.6
confidence_and_limitations: high for the fold assignment; model-based, no experimental B9D2 structure

claim_tested: Ca2+-ligand positions are conserved across ciliated eukaryotes
key_finding: Ca2+-site positions mean identity 0.43 vs 0.59 elsewhere (p=0.037); S17 0.12, I51 0.12, Q90 0.19; only D84 (0.94) and R88 (0.88) conserved, forming a 2.74 A salt bridge
confidence_and_limitations: high; 16 sequences, paralogue assignment by alignment score

claim_tested: Loop tips are basic and hydrophobic as in Ca2+-independent C2 domains
key_finding: Loops 17-24, 45-52, 80-93: 3 acidic, 2 basic, net -1, mean RSA 0.31, two exposed hydrophobic tips (I51 RSA 0.80, F86 0.71); 15 A cap has 2 K/R, fewest of 11 C2 structures (panel 3-6)
confidence_and_limitations: moderate; cap net charge alone does not separate B9D2 sharply from the panel

claim_tested: The loop pole is a constrained interaction face in the complex
key_finding: Exposed residues within 15 A of the Ca2+ site: identity 0.48 (n=15) vs 0.51 elsewhere (n=55), Mann-Whitney p=0.719; 2 of 9 conserved exposed residues at the pole, both the D84-R88 pair
confidence_and_limitations: moderate; monomer proxy because AlphaFold-Multimer could not be run

claim_tested: B9D2 contacts the TZ membrane directly
key_finding: The B9 complex interacts with and anchors TMEM67 to the TZ membrane; Joubert vs Meckel B9D2 variants separate axonemal modification from ciliogenesis defects
confidence_and_limitations: high; a protein-mediated route to the membrane that does not need lipid binding

claim_tested: B9D2 acts within an obligate protein complex
key_finding: MKS1-B9D2-B9D1 interaction order, interdependent TZ localisation, complex needed for the ciliary membrane diffusion barrier

claim_tested: B9 proteins form a complex at the ciliary base
key_finding: C. elegans XBX-7, MKSR-1, MKSR-2 form a complex at the ciliary base with interdependent localisation

claim_tested: B9 is a C2 family member
key_finding: B9 proteins (Mks1/Xbx-7, Tza-1, Tza-2) delineated as a distinct branch of the C2 superfamily in an analysis of membrane-targeting domain evolution
confidence_and_limitations: moderate; the source of the lipid framing, but family membership is not a functional assay

claim_tested: Database records assert lipid binding for B9-type C2
key_finding: The lipid sentence in PDOC51381 describes C2 domains in general; the B9 paragraph states only that these proteins are ciliary basal-body associated. PF07162 and IPR010796 have no GO term mappings
confidence_and_limitations: high for the database state as retrieved 2026-11-24
